question: What is the genetic inheritance pattern of sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Sickle cell anaemia requires two abnormal genes, one inherited from each parent, making it an autosomal recessive condition. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h1)

question: What happens to red blood cells in a person with sickle cell anaemia under low oxygen levels?

options.A: They swell and burst open immediately
options.B: They multiply faster in the bloodstream
options.C: They shrink into tiny circular discs

explanation: Low oxygen causes abnormal hemoglobin S to polymerize, turning the flexible red blood cells into stiff, crescent shapes. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h1)

question: Which amino acid replaces glutamic acid in the beta-globin chain of sickle hemoglobin?
explanation: A single point mutation replaces glutamic acid with valine, altering the physical properties of the hemoglobin molecule. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why do sickle cells cause damage to body tissues?

options.A: They stick together and block tiny blood vessels
options.B: They dissolve the walls of major arteries
options.C: They produce too much oxygen for the tissues
options.D: They absorb all available white blood cells

explanation: The rigid cells clog microcirculation, cutting off oxygen supply and causing localized tissue damage and pain. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the earliest clinical manifestation of sickle cell anaemia usually seen in toddlers?

options.A: Sudden paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Painful swelling of the hands and feet
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera

explanation: Dactylitis, or hand-foot syndrome, results from vaso-occlusion in the small bones of infants and toddlers. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why do newborn babies with sickle cell anaemia rarely show symptoms at birth?

options.A: Maternal antibodies completely prevent any sickling crisis
options.B: High levels of fetal hemoglobin protect them initially
options.C: Their bone marrow does not produce red blood cells yet
options.D: The abnormal genes remain dormant until puberty starts

explanation: Fetal hemoglobin does not interact with sickle hemoglobin polymers, delaying symptoms until fetal hemoglobin is replaced by adult hemoglobin. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which laboratory test provides definitive confirmation of hemoglobin types and variants?
explanation: Electrophoresis separates different hemoglobin types on a medium using electrical current, confirming the exact genotype. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h4)

question: When is neonatal screening most effectively integrated into routine child healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: When the child reaches secondary school age
options.B: During routine childhood immunization clinic visits
options.C: During emergency treatment for severe malaria
options.D: Only when the child is admitted for surgery

explanation: Immunization clinics bring in large numbers of infants, offering the best opportunity for early detection and counseling. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h4)

question: What is the most frequent type of crisis experienced by patients with sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Vaso-occlusive crises happen when sickled cells block blood flow, causing severe pain and remaining the most common reason for hospital admission. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h5)

question: Which infection is commonly associated with triggering an aplastic crisis in sickle cell patients?
explanation: Parvovirus B19 specifically infects red blood cell precursors in the bone marrow, halting red cell production and causing an aplastic crisis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for administering intravenous fluids during a vaso-occlusive crisis?

options.A: To reduce blood viscosity and improve microvascular flow
options.B: To prevent the development of high blood pressure
options.C: To completely suppress active bone marrow production
options.D: To raise the body temperature during a fever spike

explanation: Hydration dilutes the blood, lowering viscosity and helping red blood cells pass through narrowed vessels more easily. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h6)

question: A patient in severe sickle cell pain requests medication. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Apply ice packs to the painful joints to reduce local swelling
options.B: Wait until laboratory results confirm the exact hemoglobin level
options.C: Assess pain characteristics and administer prescribed analgesics promptly
options.D: Encourage deep breathing exercises before giving any pain relief

explanation: Prompt pain assessment and medication administration are essential for effective crisis management and patient trust. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h6)

question: How should a nurse conduct genetic counseling for couples planning to marry?

options.A: Advise them to rely entirely on prayer and spiritual fasting
options.B: Tell them to hide their test results from their extended family
options.C: Provide objective genotype information to guide their personal choices
options.D: Instruct them strictly on who they are permitted to marry

explanation: Genetic counseling is non-directive, meaning nurses provide facts and support without making decisions for the clients. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h7)

question: Which preventive measure is routinely recommended for young children diagnosed with sickle cell anaemia?

options.B: Surgical removal of the spleen at birth
options.D: Monthly blood transfusions at the clinic

explanation: Children with sickle cell anaemia take daily prophylactic medications, such as penicillin and antimalarials, to prevent severe infections. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the main goal of public health policies addressing sickle cell anaemia in Nigeria?

options.A: To improve early detection, prevention, and quality of life
options.B: To make genetic testing mandatory for all school children
options.C: To isolate affected individuals from the general population
options.D: To replace all traditional medicine with foreign treatments

explanation: Public health policies aim to reduce disease burden through screening, education, accessible treatment, and supportive care. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h8)

question: Which medication is commonly promoted in modern public health guidelines to reduce sickle cell crises?
explanation: Hydroxyurea stimulates the production of fetal hemoglobin, reducing red blood cell sickling and the frequency of painful crises. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h8)
